sentence_stem: Had the committee examined the evidence more carefully,
correct_completion: the scandal would have been avoided entirely.
full_sentence: Had the committee examined the evidence more carefully, the scandal would have been avoided entirely.
acceptable_variants: the scandal might never have occurred.
the damage to its reputation would have been prevented.

options.text: the scandal happens every single year.
options.why_wrong: The stem describes a past hypothetical, so a present habitual statement does not complete the conditional logic.

options.text: the scandal would have been avoided entirely.
the scandal will be avoided by the committee.
options.why_wrong: A future passive does not match the unreal past condition introduced by the inverted 'had' structure.

options.text: the committee was examining the evidence again.
options.why_wrong: This describes an action rather than the result of the unreal condition, so it does not complete the conditional sentence.

grammar_focus: Inverted conditional with 'had' and a perfect conditional in the main clause
explanation: The inverted 'Had ... examined' structure expresses a past hypothetical, so the main clause must use a conditional perfect form to show a result that did not happen. Learners may be tempted to choose a present or future form here, but the stem refers to a past condition.
translation: Si el comité hubiera examinado las pruebas con más cuidado, el escándalo se habría evitado por completo.
